Attention span is the amount of time spent concentrating on a task before becoming distracted. Distractibility occurs when attention is uncontrollably diverted to another stimulus or sensation.

In cognitive psychology, attention span is generally divided into transient attention, a short-term physiological response to stimuli, and sustained attention, which involves the voluntary maintenance of goal-directed focus over extended periods.
Sustained attention relies on executive function and working memory, which permit the engagement of complex analytical tasks such as structured education and long-term problem solving.

Attention span can vary significantly along the human lifespan, as it increases through childhood and adolescence alongside prefrontal cortex development. It tends to peak in middle adulthood, and gradually declines in older age. Attention span is also influenced by intrinsic motivation, the task's difficulty, fatigue, and environment.
